title: Swami Desikan's Return to Kanchipuram
body:
Swami Desikan's Return to Kanchipuram

After composing Hayagriva Stotram, Swami Desikan composed various other stotrams, such as Garuda Panchashath, a fifty-shloka treatise on Lord Garuda, Devanaayaka Panchashath, a fifty-shloka treatise on Devanatha Perumaal, and Vaikuntanaayaki Thaayar, Achyutha Shathakam, a hundred-verse stotram dealing with various ideas of philosophy. Swami Deskian has written Achyutha Shathakam using Naayika Bhavam. Naayika Bhaavam is the process of writing where one imagines oneself as a woman who is in love with the Lord. Swami Desikan composed the above stotrams and various other magnificent pieces before returning to Kanchipuram. On the way to Kanchipuram, Swami Desikan first made a stop at Tirukkovilur. At Tirukkovilur, he composed Dehaleesa Sthuthi. Dehaleesa Sthuthi is a stotram in praise of Trivikrama Perumaal, the presiding deity of this nadu naadu Divyadesam as seen through the eyes of the mudhal azhwars, namely Poigai Azhwar, Bhoothaazhwar, and Pei Azhwar. Upon returning to Kanchipuram, Swami Desikan composed Nyasa Dashakam, a ten-verse stotram on the doctrines of prapatti. Another magnum opus composed by Swami Desikan is the Artha Panchakam.

The Artha Panchakam is a set of 11 Pasurams dedicated to Sri Varadaraja Perumal of Kanchipuram. The 11 Pasurams are assigned to two each of the five doctrines or truths of the Artha Panchakam.

The five doctrines discussed  are as follows:

1. The Swarupam of Parabrahman.
2. The Swarupam of the jeevaathma.
3. The obstacles that prevent us from reaching Paramapadam
4. The means to moksham: Bhakti and Prapatti
5. The supreme goal of Bhagavat Anubhavam
